how_to_read.mass_kg: the total rigid-body mass of the asset, from the USD physics payload
how_to_read.size_m: the world-space extent of the asset's geometry, in metres (metersPerUnit is 1, up axis Z)
how_to_read.density_kg_m3: the authored material density where the asset carries one
how_to_read.materials: the semantic material labels the asset declares
how_to_read.critic_features: the critic's own six features, measured on the asset's mesh: log_volume, sphericity, elongation, fill_ratio, offcentre, defect_rate

caveats: One asset per category for most categories: the size and shape ranges are the measured spread of a single observation, not a distribution. The mass range per category is measured over every asset in that category in the dataset, under dataset_mass_kg.
category is the first underscore-delimited token of the asset's folder name, which is NVIDIA's own grouping.
mass is the sum over the asset's rigid bodies, so a multi-part asset (a forklift) carries the mass of the whole thing.

the critic's six features are computed from the signed volume of the asset's mesh, and these meshes are shells: 21 of the 38 sampled packages are not watertight, and a hollow object encloses only its wall material. The fill_ratio feature is therefore small for real objects (a mug measures 0.052 against the critic's toy mug's 0.68) and the volume-based features are not comparable with a solid-prop reference set. See docs/research/simready.md section 2.
